contentHtml:
If you're looking for one of the most unusual places in Mexico, Las Pozas in Xilitla is in a category of its own. It's a sculpture garden built in the humid jungle of the Sierra Madre Oriental, where more than eighty concrete structures stand among waterfalls and natural pools of turquoise water. Visiting Las Pozas in Xilitla means stepping into an art project without precedent in Latin America, the work of the eccentric British poet and patron of the arts Edward James.

Prices, hours and access to Las Pozas in Xilitla

How much does admission to Edward James's surrealist garden cost?

Edward James's surrealist garden doesn't sell tickets online for now: you reserve your time slot for free in the official system (up to 60 days ahead) and pay at the garden's ticket office on the day of your visit, in cash or by card. Admission is $180 MXN per adult and $120 MXN for children ages 6 to 12 and adults over 65; kids under 6 get in free. If you see $170 MXN on other websites, that was the online price in early 2026.

On top of these rates, add a mandatory $30 MXN per person for a Spanish-speaking guide (or $60 MXN if you'd like the guided visit in English). The guide isn't optional: it's part of the site's conservation protocol. If you'd rather go on a tour, the Surrealist Route, which visits Edward James's Las Pozas with pickup at your lodging in Xilitla or Ciudad Valles (from Valles, $400 MXN extra per booking), breakfast, admission and a certified guide, costs $1,400 MXN per person. You can browse options in our activities section.

Opening hours and closing days

Las Pozas is open Wednesday to Monday, 9:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m. Last entry is at 4:00 p.m., so if you arrive late you'll lose your entry even though the site is still open. It's closed on Tuesdays for conservation and maintenance work.

Since the number of visitors per day is limited, we recommend reserving your time slot online at least two or three days in advance, especially in high season (Holy Week, summer and national long weekends). To find out when the Huasteca Potosina gets fewer tourists, see our guide to the best time to visit the Huasteca Potosina.

How to get there and what to expect inside

Distance and route from Ciudad Valles

Ciudad Valles is the most common starting point for people arriving in the Huasteca Potosina by plane or bus. From there, Xilitla is 90 km away, a drive of about an hour and a half on a winding road through the mountains. The most common route is Federal Highway 120 toward Tamazunchale, taking the turnoff to Xilitla. We recommend going in your own or a rental car, although there are also colectivos (shared vans) from Ciudad Valles that leave in the morning.

Once you're in Xilitla, the way to the garden is signposted from the center of town. You can find the exact entrance on Google Maps. If you don't have a car, organized tours are more convenient. See the options in activities from Ciudad Valles.

What is there to see inside Edward James's Las Pozas?

The visit combines concrete sculptural structures—columns, staircases and arches that lead nowhere—with natural pools. The pools in the garden are for looking only: the rules prohibit swimming and going in wearing a swimsuit. When it comes to what to see in Xilitla, the top of the list is always the Stairway to Heaven, the House with Three Floors That Could Be Five, the Bamboo Palace and the Gate of Saint Peter and Saint Paul. The full guided visit takes between 90 minutes and two hours. Wear closed-toe shoes with non-slip soles for the wet stone paths.

Practical tips before visiting Las Pozas

  • Get there early: the morning light between 9:00 and 11:00 a.m. is ideal for photographing the structures before the bigger groups arrive.
  • Bring cash: the garden's ticket office takes cash or card, but some places in town only take cash.
  • The right clothes: it's humid all year, so wear light clothing and closed-toe shoes with non-slip soles. The pools in the garden are for looking, not for swimming.
  • Stay longer in Xilitla: the town has cafés, galleries and restaurants that deserve some time. You can read about Xilitla's high-altitude coffee or plan a dinner at Papán Huasteco.
  • Nearby lodging: check the lodging options in the Huasteca Potosina to choose one that fits your budget.

Follow your guide's instructions, don't touch the sculptures and stay on the marked trails. That way you help preserve this place for the people who come after you.

Where to stay near Las Pozas

To catch the first time slot without driving, stay on the road to the garden, which has no parking lot: Hotel Paraíso Encantado is a few minutes' walk from the entrance (stay right next to Las Pozas). If you're looking for other options in town, here they are compared: hotels in Xilitla.

What days is Edward James's surrealist garden open?

How do you get to Las Pozas from Ciudad Valles?

Ciudad Valles is 90 km from Xilitla, about an hour and a half by road. You can drive yourself, take a colectivo from Ciudad Valles in the morning or book a tour that includes transportation and admission.

What else is there to see in Xilitla besides Edward James's garden?

Things to see in Xilitla include the town's historic center, its high-altitude coffee shops, the local market and the Sótano de las Huahuas. Many tours combine these sights in a single day from Ciudad Valles.
